  "partial_result": "**Verdict: deployment linearity is not a causally distinct bottleneck for the deployed system, and no experiment is justified. STOP, but not because the idea was already tested here.**\n\n## Repository check: the idea is adjacent to two negatives, not closed\n\n- **Cars, UniCOM teacher, 2026-09-20.** `docs/similarity_negative_results_2026-09-19.md:287` records a matched PCA-init affine head plus a zero-init 768\u219232\u2192128 GELU residual. The residual lost mAP@R to its affine control with a bootstrap interval excluding zero, anchored and unanchored. Closed for that family only, and the doc says it does not establish that all nonlinear heads fail.\n- **In-Shop, SigLIP2-base cached features, 2026-08-13.** `docs/foundation_cached_adapter_result_2026-08-13.md` shows a 1.31M-parameter nonlinear ridge correction gaining mAP@R but almost no R@1, one seed negative, closed. The matched residual-versus-linear nested-adapter comparison was implemented at commit 350006b and never run. The doc then closed cached heads as a class and moved to image-level training.\n- **KAN head, pass 100**, died on provenance. **Token-residual gate, 2026-09-27**, was a tanh residual over token means, an information channel, not a test of the pooled-to-128 map. `docs/inshop_multidepth_head_preflight_2026-09-27.md` explicitly leaves learned nonlinear heads open.\n\nSo nothing on the SigLIP2-Large 1024-D SOP or In-Shop substrate tests a nonlinear deployment head against a matched linear control. The stop below is a mechanism stop, not a rediscovery stop.\n\n## Why linearity is not distinct in the deployed mechanism\n\nThe 1024-D source packed by `_pack_pooled` is the vision tower's pooler output. In SigLIP that pooler is the attention-pooling head: a learned probe, multi-head attention, LayerNorm, then a GELU MLP with a residual connection. The MAP head design is from Zhai et al., Scaling Vision Transformers, CVPR 2022, and is used by SigLIP, Zhai et al., ICCV 2023. I could not locate the installed transformers source read-only in this session, so that architectural fact rests on the published implementation plus the export script, which takes `pooler_output`. A ten-second grep on the training host would confirm it.\n\nThe freeze recipe leaves that pooler trainable. The SOP trainer freezes embeddings and only the first twelve blocks. The In-Shop freeze_emb arm does the same. So the trained image-to-code function class already contains every composition of an MLP head after pooling. A nonlinear head adds parameter placement and a learning-rate schedule, not a new function class. The user's linearity premise therefore describes only the cached frozen-source regime, and by the user's own rule that regime cannot identify the end-to-end mechanism.\n\nThe repository already has evidence that head-side capacity is absorbed by encoder adaptation:\n\n| Direct256 minus native128, held panel | 100 updates | 1000 updates |\n|---|---:|---:|\n| Recall@1 | +0.80 pp | +0.24 pp |\n| mAP@R | +0.0168 | +0.0080 |\n\nA nonlinear head is head-side capacity. The prediction from this pattern is a transient gain that shrinks as the upper blocks and pooler adapt.\n\n**Strongest counterargument.** Under the true-freeze recipe the pooler moves at the vision learning rate of 1e-5 for 1000 updates with weight decay, so in practice the post-token map may be close to the linear head, and a fast-moving curved head could matter. But that reframes the question as optimizer geometry and learning-rate placement, which is the loss-tweaking territory the user excluded, and the width table predicts the same fading. The memorisation channel also cuts against it: CADR found a strong fit signal with no transfer to label-disjoint pairs, and the September SOP note records a residual MLP overfitting while fit cosine rose.\n\n## The only clean test, and why it is not action-bearing\n\nA curvature-isolating design exists and is cheap: on the retained 13,283 pretrained 1024-D fit rows, use a product-disjoint inner split, train a PCA-init affine head with the existing head-first cache path, add a zero-init rank-32 GELU residual as treatment and a zero-init rank-32 affine residual as control with identical parameters, seed and schedule, and score the inner holdout with the existing packed scorer. Inference overhead would be two tiny GEMMs, under one percent of batch-1 latency, though it breaks the strict `nn.Linear` head checks in serving.\n\nIts outcomes are asymmetric. A pass cannot license training, because the trained recipe already contains the nonlinearity and a cached result cannot identify end-to-end behaviour. A fail only adds a ledger closure. That is exactly the utility objection the fit-recovery decision already adopted: a read whose outcome opens no action does not meet the stop rule. I do not recommend running it.\n\n**Frozen next action: none.** Record linearity as not causally distinct on this substrate, keep the 128-byte wire and scorer unchanged, and leave the joint goal open on substrate and information grounds rather than head form.",
